questions.stem: What kind of raw dataset do Machine Learning (ML) models normally work on?
questions.explanation: ML is about using raw but structured or semi-structured datasets, then creating feature tables of cleansed data that the models classify.

questions.stem: What kind of raw dataset do Deep Learning (DL) models work on?
options: Structured data in rows and columns
Unstructured data, where no one knows what will flow in
questions.explanation: Deep Learning models use raw but unstructured datasets where no one will know what will flow in, and dig out the required data to prepare cleansed feature tables.

questions.stem: In Machine Learning, what is a feature table?
options: A list of product features for marketing
A configuration file that lists model hyperparameters
A table no different from a traditional table, but containing cleansed data
A catalogue of image files for training
questions.explanation: Feature tables are described as no more than traditional tables but with cleansed data, which ML models then use to classify data and produce expected results.

questions.stem: Which example is used to contrast Machine Learning with Deep Learning?
options: Counting cars, bikes and buses, first from rows and columns and then from pictures
Predicting stock prices from historical trades
Detecting fraud in credit card transactions
questions.explanation: The example is counting cars, bikes or buses: easy for ML when width, length and height are in rows and columns, but pictures require Deep Learning to recognise the objects.

questions.stem: If pictures are given to a Machine Learning model to count cars, bikes and buses, what is the expected outcome?
options: It will count only the cars
It will convert the pictures to a feature table automatically
It will produce a heat map instead
It will not be possible, because ML models normally work on structured or semi-structured data
questions.explanation: The answer is No: ML models normally work on structured or semi-structured datasets, so Deep Learning algorithms and models are used to recognise objects in pictures.

questions.stem: Which type of model can recognise objects in pictures and determine whether each is a car, a bike or a bus?
questions.explanation: To find cars, bikes or buses in pictures, Deep Learning algorithms and models are used, as they can recognise the objects in the pictures.

questions.stem: What do Deep Learning models do with the unstructured dataset before classifying it?
options: Discard it and request structured data instead
Dig out the required data to prepare a cleansed dataset in the shape of feature tables
Convert it into a data warehouse
Send it to a human for manual labelling
Store it unchanged in a data lake
questions.explanation: Deep Learning models dig out required data from the unstructured dataset to prepare a cleansed dataset in the shape of feature tables, which is then classified for expected results.

questions.stem: Which measurements make it relatively easy for an ML model to count cars, bikes and buses in a structured dataset?
questions.explanation: With width, length and height available in rows and columns, ML models can easily read the dataset and produce the expected output.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Machine Learning models as described in the comparison with Deep Learning?
options: They use structured or semi-structured raw data
They rely on feature tables of cleansed data
They classify data to produce expected results
They normally recognise objects directly from pictures
They handle data in rows and columns format
questions.explanation: ML models normally work on structured or semi-structured data; recognising objects in pictures is the job of Deep Learning models.

questions.stem: After Machine Learning versus Deep Learning, what is named as the next stage of learning to understand?
questions.explanation: The comparison closes by noting that the next stage is supervised and unsupervised learning.
